title: Salsa Verde
subtitle: Italian green herb sauce with capers, anchovies, and mustard
excerpt: A bold, sharp Italian herb sauce made from parsley, capers, anchovies, garlic, mustard, and olive oil. Spoon over grilled fish, boiled meats, or roasted vegetables.

recipe.sourceNotes: Salsa verde (green sauce) is found in various forms across Italian, French, German, and Spanish cooking. The Italian version, associated particularly with Lombardy and Piedmont, uses flat-leaf parsley as the dominant herb, backed up by capers, anchovy, garlic, Dijon mustard, and olive oil. The sauce is intensely flavoured and designed to cut through rich, fatty, or bland foods: it is the traditional accompaniment to bollito misto (mixed boiled meats) in northern Italy, and it works equally well with grilled tuna, roast lamb, salt cod, or any number of vegetable dishes. The sauce should be made by hand, chopped on a board rather than blended, to preserve a coarse, slightly chunky texture: a blended salsa verde turns grey quickly and has a different character. The sauce keeps for 2 days in the fridge with a layer of olive oil over the surface.

content.text: Chop everything by hand on a large board rather than blending: the food processor produces a puree rather than a sauce, and the texture is a key part of the character. Start with the capers and anchovies and work them to a rough paste, then add the herbs and garlic and chop together until the mixture is fine but still has texture. Work in the mustard and olive oil by hand. Taste and adjust: the balance should be sharp, salty, and herby.
On a large chopping board, finely chop the capers and anchovies together to a rough paste. Add the garlic, parsley, and basil and chop everything together until fine but with some texture remaining.

Transfer to a bowl. Stir in the mustard, red wine vinegar, and olive oil. Season with a little salt (the anchovies and capers are already salty, so taste before adding). The sauce should be vivid green, sharp, and herby.
